pairs.subject: retry-backoff
pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/retry.rs:94 While with_retry_within implements jittered exponential backoff and respects stated delays, it discards attempt counts upon eventual success without recording attempts on outcomes or aggregating attempts-per-success metrics, hiding dependency degradation.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/retry.rs:106 Exponential backoff doubles delay with jitter, respects provider-stated delays, and terminates with OverBudgetWait when stated delay exceeds remaining budget.
crates/engine/src/providers.rs:320 Provider calls are dispatched through with_retry without an engine-level circuit breaker, repeatedly hammering failing providers across calls.

crates/engine/src/providers.rs:71 The HTTP client leaves redirect following to reqwest's 10-hop default without single-hop bounding or scheme downgrade checks, and retry termination is embedded in the loop.
crates/engine/src/retry.rs:19 Provider candidate generation is ephemeral in-flight evaluation work bounded by a 60-second call budget where retries appropriately live only in-memory.

crates/engine/src/providers.rs:124 Responses are mapped at the boundary into typed EngineError variants, separating transient rate limits and server errors from permanent failures and capturing stated delays.
crates/engine/src/providers.rs:367 Provider generation acts as a consumer of external LLM APIs and does not issue leased credentials requiring revocation ladders or irrevocable terminal states.
crates/engine/src/retry.rs:119 Ladder exhaustion returns the bare transient error without recording a distinct exhausted state, and successful retries discard attempt counts, hiding degradation.

crates/engine/src/providers.rs:253 Retries lack an aggregate fleet budget to cap volume, and layered fallbacks such as schema-shedding re-invoke generate_retrying, multiplying retry attempts across layers.

crates/engine/src/providers.rs:146 Connection errors are collapsed with timeouts into EngineError::Timeout and retried as transient failures, burning attempts on blocked connection attempts without suspension.

pairs.registryProposal: In multi-provider evaluation engines, distinguishing between per-request transient backoff (within engine adapters) and candidate-level circuit breaking (within matrix runners) should be clarified in the standard's scope hierarchy.
